title: Watch the sunrise

cards: Before the alarm, the window is the color of dishwater. Nothing has happened yet. Then the edge of the sky goes pale, then pink, then a color with no good name.
Birds start before there's anything to see. The rooftops come out of the dark one by one. And then, at a single point on the horizon, a sliver of fire.
Nobody pressed a button. Nobody earned it. It just arrives, as it did yesterday and the day before, mostly while people sleep.

teach.b: Today the practice is the lesson: watch one sunrise, all the way through. First, why it works on people. A sunrise is vast and slow.
You can't hurry it or pause it. For once, the day comes to you, instead of you chasing the day. Second, in several traditions, the hours around dawn hold a special place in prayer.
Muslims pray the dawn prayer, Fajr, before the sun comes up.
Jews say the morning prayers of Shacharit as the day begins. Some Hindus offer water to the rising sun.
Each tradition has its own reasons, and they aren't the same reasons, but each gathers near the hours when the light changes. Third, a poet's picture.

In the Psalms, the sun comes out "as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race." A wedding and a race at once, as if the sun had been waiting all night to begin.

teach.h: ONLY THAT DAY DAWNS TO WHICH WE ARE AWAKE.
teach.b: Near the very end of Walden he writes a line about dawn that isn't about the sky at all: "Only that day dawns to which we are awake." The sun comes up whether anyone is watching.
But a day you sleep through, in body or in attention, never quite dawns for you. Watching a sunrise is a way of being awake for one, on purpose, start to finish.
It arrives. The only question is whether anyone is there to meet it.

how: People who make a practice of watching the sunrise get up before dawn, go somewhere with a view of the eastern sky, and watch quietly from first light until the sun is up; in several traditions, morning prayers gather around the hours of dawn.

games.why: the practice is the whole arrival: the dark, the pale edge, the colors, and the first sliver of sun.

practice: Turn toward the brightest window you have; if the sky is changing, watch it, and if not, close your eyes and bring back a sunrise you've seen or can imagine.
Follow it slowly, the dark, the pale edge, the colors, the first sliver, without rushing to the end. Let the light come to you, and breathe as if you have all the time it takes.

wordCard.voice: Fajr. The Muslim dawn prayer, said before the sun comes up, one of several traditions' ways of greeting the whole arrival of a day. Today's word.
